dream_job.statement: My next role is the one where I get to focus on the hard parts of event-driven systems: designing and running reliable data pipelines, building the tooling and APIs that other engineers depend on, and making Kafka and Kubernetes behave at scale. Day to day, that looks like sketching the topology for a new flow, sitting in front of my own logs and Grafana dashboards, maybe pairing with a backend engineer on a nasty concurrency bug, and then writing the small, brave Go service that holds the whole thing together. I want to work in a product company with a pragmatic cloud-native culture, where streaming is the default and batch is the exception. The team should be small but senior, with enough ownership to take services to production without a rewrite every quarter. I need to collaborate with platform engineers and SREs, not just be handed a ticket. What I want to stop doing: front-end work, chasing flaky CI, and being the last line of defense for production incidents that could have been prevented by better design. I won't take a role where I'm expected to write React or fix CSS. No more babysitting flaky CI pipelines whose failures we never investigate. And I need a team that owns its incidents end-to-end, not one that just pages me in the middle of the night.

planted_conflicts.why: The CV states the legal entity, the export states the brand. The merge still pairs the role because company_variants strips the legal form, so the disagreement is reported rather than read as two separate jobs.

The CV ends the role three months before the export does - the ordinary drift of a CV rewritten from memory. Both readings are month-precise, so _same_date reports a real disagreement rather than a rounding gap.
